pullRequests.scope: Read-only independent review; no merge, close, branch deletion, dependency change or CI trigger
pullRequests.policy: Main can be the one permanent human development branch while eight temporary automated dependency branches remain attached to unresolved PRs.
pullRequests.interpretation: MERGE_LATER means eligible for a separate authorized update only after current-main validation; it is not merge approval and no PR is fully certified by this read-only review. DEFER means retain PR/branch while a concrete compatibility/policy blocker is unresolved. No CLOSE_AS_UNNECESSARY recommendation is warranted from the reviewed evidence.
pullRequests.checkLimits: Check-run totals can include both push and pull-request events; the per-PR workflow conclusions identify actual PR runs. Historical failures/cancellations do not prove current product defects. Metadata mergeability is unknown and is not a merge decision.

32 exercise records with all written execution sequences, mistakes, programming contexts, source/review metadata, local diagrams and metadata-based filtering.
32 science topics with evidence/limitations and exercise links; 25 cite ACSM 2026 sources, including the actual position stand (not just older guidance).

4 published programs: two NIA foundation templates and two NHS general-fitness templates. Finder/comparison/current selection preserve source scope, unknown time, version pins, local weekdays and approved substitutions.
Existing tracker supports ad hoc/repeated/program-based workouts, personal labels, set/performance edits, exercise reordering, history, timer, backup/restore and CSV.
uxGaps: Region selector is a navigation cue; no per-muscle visual location/action explanation or muscle-role legend links the abstract body into a guided lesson.
Users navigate among muscle, exercise, science, program and tracker pages manually; no single bounded learn→choose→save-plan→start flow.
Static cue SVGs, some predominantly text panels, do not show movement/position changes or provide structured start/middle/end guidance states.
Role metadata is mostly context-dependent; primary/secondary activation graphics cannot truthfully be auto-filled. Cards show related names; qualifiers are chiefly in detail text.
The existing program selector customizes a published template; ad hoc/repeat sessions are not a saved editable user-authored multi-session workout-plan builder.
educationalGaps: 0 muscle-specific media bindings; optional trainingRelevance and misconceptions are empty across current raw muscle records.

3 group records omit structure and 7 subdivision records omit joint-action arrays; not automatically defects and do not fill by inference.

pilot.title: One guided six-exercise learn-to-plan pilot
pilot.scope: The six already-published exercises used by program_full_body_2_day_foundation; at most two user-authored sessions; twelve currently linked muscle IDs; one existing tracker integration. Do not publish new factual identities or activate the 900-item backlog.
priorities: First create original labelled location/action schematics for only the twelve existing linked muscle records, with mirrored text and explicit approximate/not-to-scale labels; use existing sourced facts and preserve role qualifiers. Any precision claim beyond those sources requires actual review before publication.

For the six exercise pages, provide accessible user-controlled setup/action/reset views derived from current execution text/diagrams, visible source links, existing difficulty/equipment and stop signals. No autoplay, video dependency or fabricated posture measurement.

Add a local-only draft plan capped at two sessions, composed only of the six allowlisted IDs, with title, reorder/edit/delete, user-entered sets/reps/rest (or explicitly attributed canonical targets if cloned) and an explicit reviewed-source/custom-change distinction. Do not generate prescriptions from goals/health data or call a user plan a reviewed canonical program.

Save in IndexedDB behind an explicitly reviewed local record contract, version/snapshot semantics, validation-before-write and backup/restore/CSV coverage. Start a session through existing tracker primitives; do not fork a second logging system.
acceptance: Dataset count/hash freeze: 70 muscles,32 exercises,32 science,4 programs and 900 backlog unchanged; no new published fitness entities.

All six exercise→muscle links resolve by immutable ID. Every existing primary/context-dependent/stabilizer role and source qualifier is preserved; no EMG percentages, secondary roles or isolation claims invented.
Every new original visual has stable ID, source/author/license/review metadata, useful text alternative and a source-backed scope. No new human-review date without an actual review.

A keyboard/mobile user can select a taught region, read one of six guides, add exercises to a draft, reorder, explicitly enter targets, save, reload, edit/delete, start in the current tracker and return to the plan without losing records.
Canonical program content/version and completed workout snapshots remain unchanged when the local plan is edited. Unknown duration/rest stays unavailable until user-supplied, not zero or guessed.

Plan export/import round trip succeeds, CSV includes plan data, malformed imports cause zero writes, rollback/error feedback preserves old records, and destructive replacement/deletion requires confirmation.
Personal data stays browser-local and absent from SSR/logs/URLs/metadata/network. No accounts, cloud storage or external fitness runtime API.

Semantic controls, visible focus, role/state alternatives and reduced motion; desktop/mobile Light/Dark/Auto focused axe/keyboard checks and required app gates after future implementation. Do not run broad suites during this documentation task.

acsm.boundedInterpretation: The 2026 position stand concerns resistance-training outcomes in healthy adults and differentiates goal-specific variables; the ACSM release emphasizes regular participation and individualized, maintainable plans. This supports a simple user-controlled plan and clear scope, not an automatic universal load/volume prescription. Existing science already references these sources. No new factual content was published and no literature expansion is proposed.
